LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.3: Phonological Awareness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Phonological Awareness. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you make clear descriptions in oral communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Phonological Awareness means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Phonological Awareness from Kenya
3. practise Phonological Awareness in clear steps
4. apply Phonological Awareness in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Phonological Awareness helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school and at home in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS
Study Phonological Awareness like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Phonological Awareness means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Phonological Awareness means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Phonological Awareness means in simple pupil language.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Phonological Awareness” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Phonological Awareness means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Phonological Awareness from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Phonological Awareness from Kenya. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Phonological Awareness from Kenya.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Show one correct way to practise Phonological Awareness.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Phonological Awareness from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Phonological Awareness in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Phonological Awareness in clear steps. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Phonological Awareness in clear steps.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Phonological Awareness in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Phonological Awareness in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Phonological Awareness in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Phonological Awareness in one real-life situation this week.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Phonological Awareness” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Phonological Awareness in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Phonological Awareness is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Explain “Phonological Awareness” in your own words using one local example. (skill: explain what Phonological Awareness means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Show one correct way to practise Phonological Awareness. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Phonological Awareness from Kenya)

Example 3: Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson. (skill: practise Phonological Awareness in clear steps)

Example 4: Explain “Phonological Awareness” in your own words using one local example. (skill: apply Phonological Awareness in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Phonological Awareness to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Phonological Awareness means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Phonological Awareness from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Phonological Awareness in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Phonological Awareness from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Phonological Awareness: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Phonological Awareness?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you make clear descriptions in oral communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Phonological Awareness means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Phonological Awareness means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Phonological Awareness from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
